title: NHC 7-day tropical cyclone formation probabilities were 1.2 times too low in 2023-2026, mainly for disturbances not yet formed and for days 3-7; 2-day values had no clear total bias
abstract: We tested the formation probabilities of the US National Hurricane Center Tropical Weather Outlook with a pre-registered plan (written and timestamped before any comparison). We rebuilt all public outlooks from the NHC GIS archive for May 2023 to November 2026 (Atlantic and eastern North Pacific): 3,098 six-hour cycles, 5,153 outlook-disturbance units in 280 linked disturbance chains. We compared them with 142 formations in HURDAT2 (2023-2025) and in operational ATCF best tracks (2026). Intervals are 95% bootstrap intervals over whole chains. The 2-day probabilities had no clear total bias (observed/expected 0.94, 0.83-1.05), but stated 10-30% values were too high (0.66, 0.50-0.84). The 7-day probabilities were too low: 1.22 (1.12-1.33), with 1.22 in each basin and an excess in all four seasons. Stated 20% verified 34% of the time; stated 70-100% was near correct. The deficit came from two connected sources. For areas with no existing disturbance (a low expected to form) the ratio was 1.70 (1.51-1.91), against 1.08 (0.97-1.18) for existing disturbances. When no formation occurred by 48 h, the implied chance for days 3-7 was too low by 1.46 times (1.31-1.63). The outlooks put 46% of the 7-day probability in the first 48 h, but only 36% of formations occurred there. In a pre-registered efficiency test, a 10-point rise of the probability in the past 24 h increased the log-odds of formation at a fixed stated value (+0.23, 0.13-0.32, 7-day; +0.20, 0.07-0.33, 2-day). Thus the forecasts moved too slowly. A leave-one-season-out recalibration that uses the 7-day and 2-day values, an area-only flag and the basin reduced the 7-day Brier score by 10.7% (4.4-17.1%). The results held under five matching rules and a strict same-chain rule. Our 2024 counts match the NHC verification tables in the 20-90% bins, but the NHC tables contain about 280 more 10% (7-day) forecasts than the public products; these extra forecasts verified near 25%. Limitations: public geometry replaces the NHC internal disturbance database; large polygons allow chance matches (a year-shift placebo bound keeps the area-only result but not the small excess for existing disturbances); 2026 outcomes are preliminary; only four seasons; the timing, placebo and recalibration analyses are post hoc.

display.caption: Reliability of NHC 2-day (left) and 7-day (right) formation probabilities, May 2023 to Nov 2026, Atlantic (blue) and East Pacific (orange). Points: observed frequency per stated 10% value; bars: 95% bootstrap over disturbance chains. Lower panels: number of units. The 7-day values from 20% to 60% verified more often than stated.

Stated (open diamond) and observed (blue, 95% CI) probability of formation within 48 h (left) and in 48-168 h when none occurred by 48 h (right), by disturbance group. Areas without an existing disturbance and days 3-7 carry the 7-day deficit; low 2-day values for weak disturbances were too high.

Observed frequency against stated probability, split by the 24-h change of the same disturbance's probability (both basins). At equal stated values, rising probabilities verified more often than falling ones: the issued values move too slowly.
